svg.title: The word-vector table and the docent trained on it
svg.desc: The Engram-style hashed table (rows for vocabulary words at the docent's hash slots, small random rows elsewhere), with the held-out destination accuracy and validation loss over epochs for the fine-tuned and the frozen table, each trained in its own process.
svg.text: HASHED TABLE -- vectors at the docent's slots, then the docent on top
WHAT: 1024 rows of 24: 474 hold vocabulary vectors (112 words collided into an occupied row); the rest are random at 0.05 scale.
0 .. 1 over 40 epochs, every 5; amber fine-tuned table, pink frozen
example rows of the table, first 8 of 24 values (apl and cosmac before fine-tuning)
WHY: an Engram-style table is addressed by a hash of the input, not by a dictionary, so unseen words still land on a row;
here the rows start as meaning (word vectors) instead of noise, and fine-tuning may keep or erase that meaning.
HOW: docent_table is a param [1024, 24] assigned the table; u:docent_pooled_t gathers rows (gather_rows is differentiable,
finding F4) and averages them; the frozen run lists only the body and heads in adam. One process per variant (F22).
WHAT DECIDES: the paraphrase columns in the docent results table against MB01t; the bar needs plus 20 points.
Bigram slots have no vectors (random rows); word rows shared by hash collisions carry the last word written.
